JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that, on 14.03.2022 at about 8.30 a.m, when the petitioner was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JC-3653 on the extreme left side of the Kolar - Bengaluru NH-75 road, by observing all the traffic rules and regulations when he reached near Medahalli, on Kolar- Bengaluru NH-75 road, Bengaluru City, the driver of Hyundai i20 car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-ME- 8735 driven the same at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life and without giving any signal or indication all of a suddenly he steered the car towards his left side to go towards service road.
As a result he lost control over the vehicle, went to its wrong side of the road and dashed violently against the petitioner's motorcycle.
Because of the accident the petitioner fell down on the road along with his motorcycle and sustained many injuries.
It is further urged that, immediately after the accident he was shifted to Government Hospital, K.R.Puram wherein he took treatment as an outpatient.
Later he has taken treatment at Sanjay Gandhi Hospital, Bengaluru wherein he was treated as inpatient and underwent surgery.
He has spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards treatment and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that, due to the accidental injuries he is unable to work as such he suffered both financially and emotionally.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of car.
The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the car and they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation, as such prayed to grant a compensation amount.
3. Notice was duly served to respondent No.1.
Respondent No.1 appeared through his counsel, he failed to contest the matter by filing the written statement.
4. The respondent No.2 appeared through his counsel and filed written statement denied the issuance of insurance policy in respect of car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-ME-8735.
However the liability if any is pleaded to be subject to the terms & conditions of the policy.
It is also urged that there is inordinate delay of 35 days that itself vibrantly discloses that the case is foisted so as to wangle the compensation amount from the respondents.
This respondent specifically and empathically denied the occurrence, mode and manner of accident and also involvement of the vehicle in the accident.
Negligence on the part of the driver of car is denied by this respondent.

Per contra it is alleged that the petitioner who was riding the motorcycle without having a proper lookout at the vehicular movement on the road and he was solely responsible for the occurrence of the accident.
In fact the petitioner was also not wearing helmet and also not possessing valid DL at the time of alleged accident.
Without prejudice to the said contention it is averred that the driver of the car did not possess valid & effective DL as on the date of accident.

On account of willful breach of the terms &
conditions of the policy by the insured, the insurance company is not liable to indemnify him.
Non -compliance of section's 134(c), 158(6), 147, 149(2) of MV Act is pleaded.
Rest of the petition averments are contended as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues were framed :
Sandesh.A vs T.G. Santhosh Kumar on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164353905/
2 ISSUES 1) Whether the petitioner proves that on 14.03.2022 at about 8.30 a.m, while the petitioner was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JC-3653 and when he reached near Medehalli, on Kolar - Bengaluru NH-75 road, Bidarahalli Hobli, Bengaluru East Taluk, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Hyundai i20 car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-ME-8735 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner's motorcycle.
As a result, the petitioner fell down from the motorcycle and sustained grievous injuries ?

2) Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3) What order or award ?
6. The petitioner examined himself as PW.1.
Ex's.P1 to 13 were marked on his behalf.
In order to prove the defence, respondent No.2 examined the Doctor, Government Hospital, K.R.Puram as RW.1 and through him got marked Ex.R.1 & 2.

Further the Legal Manager of the respondent No.2 insurance company has examined as RW.2.
7.
Heard erudite counsel for the petitioners and respondent No.2 counsel on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows:-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 :
The petitioner has knocked the doors of justice with a relief to grant a compensation of an amount to the tune of Rs.10,00,000/- together.

It is the specific contention of the respondent No.2 is that there is delay of 35 days in filing the FIR as such the petitioner in active collusion with respondent No.1 and police officials have falsely implicated the insured vehicle.
When this being the specific contention urged by the respondent No.2 it is relevant to fall back on the documentary and oral evidence placed before this court.
According to the version of the petitioner, the accident happened on 14.03.2022 at about 8.30 a.m.
The complaint was filed on 18.04.2022 at about 3.15 p.m.
There is approximately 35 days delay in filing the FIR.
It is relevant to note that Ex.P.2 was filed by the petitioner himself.

The alleged delay is suitable explained by the complainant in Ex.P.2.
9.
In order to falsify the contention of petitioner, the respondent No.2 have also got summoned the doctor of Government Hospital, K.R.Puram who had written the MLC and examined as RW.1.
He has also produced Ex.R.1 & 2 being the MLC extract and Police intimation.
In his chief-examination RW.1 stated that MLC was done on 07.04.2022 at around 4.10 p.m, with regard to one Sandesh.
A to their hospital
with an history of RTA which had happened on 14.03.2022.

As the witness is turned Sandesh.A vs T.G. Santhosh Kumar on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164353905/
3 hostile and counsel for respondent seeking permission to cross examined RW.1.
During the course of cross examination RW.1 stated that on 14.03.2022 petitioner came to the hospital and complain of the shoulder pain and he had taken treatment and went away.
Further he stated that on 14.03.2022 the petitioner did not complain of RTA as per contents of Ex.P.9.
Further RW.1 stated that, as the petitioner stated that he could not enter compromise with respondent No.1 as such the RW.1 recorded the MLC as per Ex.R.1.
During the course of cross examination of counsel for petitioner RW.1 stated that Ex.P.9 is issued by their hospital.

On perusal of Ex.P.9 Out patient record (Token No.1) the petitioner has visited the hospital after the accident i.e., on 14.03.2022 at about 9:45:04 a.m., in the said document it is not mentioned the RTA.

Further on perusal of Out patient record Re-visit document (token No.70) the petitioner has visited the said hospital on 07.04.2022 at about 03:28:28 p.m.
10.
Further the respondent No.2 has also examined its official as RW.2.
During the course of cross examination he stated that he has deposed based on the documents and he has not have any personal knowledge about this accident.
He further admitted that police have filed charge sheet and they have not challenged the same.
Further he admitted that they have collected the police documents and they have not enquired any eye-witnesses.
11. On careful perusal of the Ex.R.1 & 2 i.e, MLC and Police intimation it reflects that, the police intimation was sent to the jurisdictional police on 07.04.2022 at about 4.10 p.m itself.
Added more Ex.R.1 being the MLC register extract also discloses that the petitioner on 14.03.2022 was proceeding as a rider hit by car.
These two documents cures the factum of delay.

This court will also does not loose sight of the fact that, the cause of delay in setting criminal law into motion is ventilated in Ex.P.2 being FIR wherein the driver of the car had hit the petitioner vehicle and ran away.
During the course of cross examination PW.1 categorically admitted that the car caused the accident and ran away.
After the accident he has taken photograph of offending car.
Further the RW.1 in his cross examination also admitted that the petitioner has shown the vehicle number in mobile.
The same is mentioned in Ex.R.1.
When such being the case this court cannot found fault with the mere delay of 35 days in lodging FIR.

In this regard it is relevant to relay on the decision reported in (2011) 4 SCC 693, in the case of Ravi v/s Bhadrinarayana and others, wherein it is held that "It is well-settled that delay in lodging FIR cannot be a ground to doubt the claimant's case.
Knowing the Indian conditions as they are, we cannot expect a common man to first rush to the Police Station immediately after an accident.
Human nature and family responsibilities occupy the mind of kith and kin to such an extent that they give more importance to get the victim treated rather than to rush to the Police Station''.
Under such circumstances, they are not expected to act mechanically with promptitude in lodging the FIR with the Police.
Delay in lodging the FIR thus,
cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
In cases of delay, the courts are required to examine the evidence with a closer scrutiny and in doing so; the contents of the FIR should also be scrutinized more carefully.

If court finds that there is no indication of fabrication or it has not been concocted or engineered to implicate innocent persons then, even if there is a delay in lodging the FIR, the claim case cannot be dismissed merely on that ground.
The principles reiterated in the above decision squarely applicable to the facts of the instant case.
The ratio decidendi laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court is aptly applicable to the facts of the instant case.
The petitioner clearly demonstrated as to the involvement of the offending vehicle in the accident.

It seems that after the Sandesh.A vs T.G. Santhosh Kumar on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164353905/
4 accident the driver of the said car agreed to pay the medical expenses, when he failed to pay and when it was more expensive then 12.

In order to prove actionable negligence on part of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-05-JC-3653 the petitioner who examined himself as PW.1, has relied upon the police documents marked at Ex's.P.1 to 7.
Ex. P.1
- FIR &
Ex.P.2- Complaint
corroborate the occurrence and information of the accident.
The contents of Spot Mahazar make it clear that the accident occurred due to the rash & negligent act of the driver of car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-ME-8735.
Ex.P.6-Wound certificate discloses that the petitioner sustained simple injuries in a road traffic Accident.
The IMV report goes to show that at the time of inspection both the vehicles involved in the accident had sustained damages as detailed out in the said report.
Be that as it may, the IMV inspector has mentioned that he tested the vehicles on road and found that their brake systems were in order.
He has thereby opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said vehicles.
Therefore the driver of car did not have sufficient cause to cause the accident.
The fact that yet he went and dashed against the motorcycle leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle rashly and negligently.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed chargesheet against him for the offences punishable u/s 187 of IMV Act and 279, 337 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
13. Perusal of the cross-examination by the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2 goes to show that the factum of accident is not denied by the Insurance Company.

Only suggestions were made to the effect that the alleged accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of petitioner,
which were out rightly denied.
Except putting in this suggestion, nothing worthwhile was elicited from PW.1's mouth to dislodge the ocular and documentary evidence adduced on his behalf.
14. Though the respondent No.1 appeared but did not chosen to file his written statement by contesting the petition.
Accordingly an adverse inference could be drawn against him that he has impliedly admitted the petition averments.
Though the respondent No.2 denied the cause of the accident, it has not let in any cogent evidence to prove its defence.
Further, the Insurance Company did not make any attempt to examine the driver of its insured vehicle, who is the best witness to depose about the cause of accident.
There is no explanation to that effect.
Non-examination of the said driver is fatal to the defence of respondent No.2.
Hence its contention that there was no negligence on the part of driver of the car has to be disbelieved.
Under such circumstances the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by police documents has to be accepted.
Consequently I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the negligence of the driver of the car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-ME-8735.

In addenda, in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2011) 3 SCC 646.

With this observation issue No.1 is answered as 'In the Affirmative'.
15. ISSUE NO.2 : As per the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : i)
Tenderness over left hand (ii) MRI mild shoulder joint effusion, which are opined to be simple in nature.
Ex. P.9
Out patient record of General Hospital, K.R.Puram which discloses that the petitioner has taken treatment as an outpatient on the same day of accident itself.

The discharge Sandesh.A vs T.G. Santhosh Kumar on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164353905/
5 summary as per Ex.P8 of Sanjay Gandhi Institute of Trauma, Bengaluru indicates that the petitioner was treated as an inpatient in the said hospital for the period from 27.05.2022 to 01.06.2022 (6 days in total).

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: During the course of treatment he had undergone surgeries in the form of : Left arthroscopic rotater cuff repair done on 30.05.2022 under GA.
16. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY & LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID-UP PERIOD :
It is the case of the petitioner that the accidental injuries have caused him permanent disability.
However he has neither examined the doctor nor produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact he has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that the petitioner has suffered permanent disability.

17. As per the averments made in his evidence affidavit, at the time of accident the petitioner was working as a Assistant Master at Shree Venkateshwara English Nursery, Primary and High School,
K.R.Puram and thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.a.

entities.text:
Shree Venkateshwara English Nursery, Primary and High School,
K.R.Puram
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: In order to substantiate the above said fact the petitioner has produced his salary certificate as per Ex.P10.
It is the specific defence of the respondent that the petitioner had continued his service as a school teacher, when such being a case there is no question of loss of future income.

In order to substantiate the above said fact the respondent No.2 counsel had relied on the categorical admission of PW1 during the course of cross- examination which reads as hereunder :
"It is true that Ex.P.10 prepared with intention to produce before court.
My salary was credited to my bank account.
I have bank account in Canara Bank.
I can produce my accounts statement.
At present also I am employee of said school.
It is true that after accident also I obtained salary."
Further it could be ascertained from the cross examination of PW.1 that at present the petitioner is working in school.
According to the version of the petitioner himself that prior to the accident he was working as teacher and also after the accident he has obtained salary.

In this regard it is relevant to relied on decision reported in ILR 2010 KAR 2439 in the case of Sri. Subhash V/s New India Assurance Co.Ltd, wherein it was held that 'If the claimant has continued in service, then the question of awarding compensation towards loss of future income does not arise.'

entities.text: Sri. Subhash V/s New India Assurance Co.Ltd
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore no compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the heads of 'Loss of future income due to disability' and 'loss of income during laid-up period'.
18. ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The period of hospitalization of 6 days is proved.

During his stay in the hospital the petitioner would have incurred expenses towards attendant charges as some family member of the petitioner would have accompanied her to the hospital to take him care by leaving their duties.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have also spent a considerable amount towards special diet, transportation and nutrition.
Considering the rate of inflation and rise in the price index, the same is quantified at Rs.1,500/- per day and a sum of Rs.9,000/- (1,500 X 6) is awarded under this head.

Sandesh.A vs T.G. Santhosh Kumar on 1 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164353905/
6 19.
PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
On account of the accidental injuries the petitioner would have had undergone pain and mental agony.
Thus this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.50,000/- under this head.
20. MEDICAL EXPENSES:

As per the bills marked at Ex.P11, the petitioner has spent Rs.55,865/-
towards medical expenses.
Nothing worthwhile was elicited during the course of her cross-examination, so as to doubt the genuineness of these bills.
Hence the petitioner is entitled for Rs.55,865/- which is rounded off to Rs.55,900/- towards medical expenses.
21. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The disability referred above would have necessarily caused physical deformity with which the petitioner has to live the rest of his life.
Hence a sum of Rs.40,000/- is awarded under this head.
22. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
No evidence is brought on record to demonstrate the requirement for further treatment and the medical & incidental expenses to be incurred therefrom.
In the absence of proof no amount is awarded under this head.

23. The calculation table stands as follows:
1 Loss of future income due to : - Nil - disability 2 Loss of income during laid-up : -
Nil - period 3 Attendant charges, extra : 9,000-00 nutritious food & conveyance charges 4 Pain & sufferings : 50,000-00 5
Medical expenses : 55,900-00 6 Loss of future amenities & : 40,000-00 happiness 7
Future medical expenses : - Nil - Total 1,54,900-00 24.
INTEREST & LIABILITY:

Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a,
is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
25. It is contended in para 2 of the written statement that, respondent.No.2 has not issued any policy.

However careful perusal of policy which is found in documents as per the contents of which the issuance of insurance policy is respect of Hyundai i20 Car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-ME-8735 covering the date of accident.
Hence, there is no dispute with regard to the issuance of insurance policy and its validity as on the date of accident.

Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the owner of the Hyundai i20 Car bearing Reg.No.KA-53-ME-8735 and respondent No.1 being the insurer thereof are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
Hence this issue is answered as 'Partly in the Affirmative'.

7 26.
ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER
The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,54,900/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the aforesaid award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.
After deposit, the entire award amount together with interest, shall be released to the petitioner by way of E-payment on proper identification and confirmation.

Out of the above said compensation amount awarded to the petitioner, 80% of the award amount with accrued interest shall be paid to him through NEFT/RTGS by way of E-payment on proper identification and due verification and further 20% of the award amount shall be kept in FD in favour of petitioner in any Nationalized or Scheduled bank for a period of 3 years.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
